source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 5: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Proper rational function hai: upar degree 1, neeche degree 2.
Denominator \(4 + 5x - 6x^2\) ko factorise karna hai; is ke factors \(4 - 3x\) aur \(1 + 2x\) bante hain, dono linear aur alag, yani Case-I.
Is sawal ki khaas baat: factors mein \(x\) ke saath coefficient (\(-3\) aur 2) hai, is liye integral karte waqt \(\frac{1}{a}\) ka khayal rakhna hoga.
Plan: factorise, roots \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) aur \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) rakh kar \(A\), \(B\), phir dhyan se integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{3 - 16x}{4 + 5x - 6x^2}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: denominator factorise, partial fractions (Case-I), aur formula \(\int \frac{dx}{ax + b} = \frac{1}{a}\ln|ax + b|\). Yeh formula is liye chahiye ke \(ax + b\) ka derivative \(a\) hai, 1 nahi; \(\frac{1}{a}\) us kami ko poora karta hai.

Denominator factorise karein
\[4 + 5x - 6x^2 = (4 - 3x)(1 + 2x)\]
Kyun: Khud expand kar ke tasalli kijiye: \(4 + 8x - 3x - 6x^2 = 4 + 5x - 6x^2\). Agar shakal mushkil lage to \(-(6x^2 - 5x - 4) = -(3x - 4)(2x + 1)\) se bhi yahi milta hai.

Partial fractions
\[\dfrac{3 - 16x}{(4 - 3x)(1 + 2x)} = \dfrac{A}{4 - 3x} + \dfrac{B}{1 + 2x}\]
\[3 - 16x = A(1 + 2x) + B(4 - 3x) \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Har linear factor ke neeche ek constant; phir poore denominator se multiply kar ke fractions khatam.

(1) mein \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) rakhein
\[3 - \dfrac{64}{3} = A\left(1 + \dfrac{8}{3}\right)\]
\[-\dfrac{55}{3} = \dfrac{11}{3}A\]
\[A = -5\]
Kyun: \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) par \(4 - 3x = 0\), is liye \(B\) wala term gayab. \(16 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{64}{3}\) aur \(3 = \frac{9}{3}\), to \(\frac{9 - 64}{3} = -\frac{55}{3}\). Dono taraf \(\frac{11}{3}\) se divide kiya: \(A = -5\).

(1) mein \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) rakhein
\[3 + 8 = B\left(4 + \dfrac{3}{2}\right)\]
\[11 = \dfrac{11}{2}B\]
\[B = 2\]
Kyun: \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\) par \(1 + 2x = 0\). \(-16 \times (-\frac{1}{2}) = +8\) aur \(-3 \times (-\frac{1}{2}) = +\frac{3}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: Fraction wale roots se ghabrayein nahi; bas dhyan se signs lagayein.

Integral lein
\[\int \left(\dfrac{-5}{4 - 3x} + \dfrac{2}{1 + 2x}\right)dx\]
\[= -5\cdot\dfrac{\ln|4 - 3x|}{-3} + 2\cdot\dfrac{\ln|1 + 2x|}{2}\]
\[= \dfrac{5}{3}\ln|4 - 3x| + \ln|2x + 1| + c\]
Kyun: \(4 - 3x\) mein \(a = -3\), is liye \(\frac{1}{-3}\) aaya; \(-5 \times \frac{1}{-3} = \frac{5}{3}\) (do minus mil kar plus). \(1 + 2x\) mein \(a = 2\), aur \(2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{1}{a}\) bhool jayein to jawab \(-5\ln|4 - 3x|\) aa jata hai, jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\dfrac{5}{3}\ln|4 - 3x| = \dfrac{5}{3}\cdot\dfrac{-3}{4 - 3x} = \dfrac{-5}{4 - 3x}\]
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\ln|2x + 1| = \dfrac{2}{2x + 1}\]
Kyun: Chain rule se andar wale \(4 - 3x\) ka derivative \(-3\) bahar aaya. Dono derivatives wapas wohi partial fractions de rahe hain, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 301) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (v) hai: \(\frac{5}{3}\ln|4 - 3x| + \ln|2x + 1| + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
